newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine privatisation body eyes foreign investors.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine privatisation body eyes foreign investors.

text.p: Ukraine's state privatisation agency, the State Property Fund (FDM), plans to offer more to foreign investors in 1997, its deputy chairman told a conference on Wednesday.
"Part of our plan will be to offer more attractive large blocks of shares to outsiders," Yevhen Hryhorenko told a meeting sponsored by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Ukraine.
Parliament is expected to approve the FDM's 1997 plan once it approves a new chief to replace Yuri Yekhanurov, appointed Economy Minister last month.
"We are very interested in the active participation of foreign investors in Ukrainian privatisation," Hryhorenko said.
He said that between 150 and 200 joint-stock companies would be created each month this year, and that their shares would be traded on Ukraine's young securities market.
"The securities market is an unploughed field," he said.

The market consists of the Ukrainian Stock Exchange, the Ukrainian Interbank Currency Exchange, the Kyiv International Stock Exchange, the Donetsk Stock Exchange and a Kiev-based over-the-counter stock system.
The country has nearly completed small-scale and is proceeding with medium- and large-scale privatisation, including a list of enterprises deemed "strategic" to national security.
